# ⚠️ Verified routing clarification (read first)

The single fact that scopes the whole gap, verified directly in code:

`server/rails-router.ts:301` — `if (isLoopsEnabled() && loopId) → LoopRunManager (loop.run_*, no jobId); else → QueueManager (jobId, rail.job_*)`.

- **Phone-initiated launches** send bare `{mode}` with **no `loopId`** (`desktop_repository.dart:116-123`) → fall to the **`else` / QueueManager** path → real `jobId` → `rail.job_*` → **the v1 companion mirrors them correctly (view + log tail + completion push). NO regression.**
- **Desktop-initiated launches** now **always** send a `loopId`: the loop picker uses `effectiveLoopId = selectedLoopId || factoryIdForMode(mode)` (`client/src/lib/rail-loops.ts:43-44`) so even a plain "Implement" rail sends `loopId='factory:implement'`, and `doLaunchRail` always passes it (`client/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:824,869`) → **LoopRunManager** → `loop.run_*` (no `jobId`) → **dropped at the mobile boundary** (`mobile-ws.ts topicFor` default→null).

**Net:** the mirror gap is NOT in the phone's own launches — it is in **mirroring rails the user launches from the desktop** (the normal case), which now emit `loop.run_*` the boundary never forwards. So a connected phone shows desktop-launched loop rails as **idle, with no live progress and no completion notification.** The frozen wire is untouched (additive only). Everything below stands with this scoping.

---

# Rails-as-Loops: Companion Mirror Contract-Change Report

## 1. Mirror contract today — what the companion relies on for rails

The companion is a **light-control mirror**. It has no typed `Rail` model: rails are consumed as untyped `Map<String,dynamic>`. The contract it actually depends on, concretely:

**REST (the `/v1` proxy in `server/mobile/mobile-router.ts`):**
- `GET /v1/projects/:pid/rails` → companion `desktop_repository.dart:71-88` reads `{ rails: [...], activeJobs: {railIndex→{jobId,mode}} }`. It folds `activeJobs` into a synthetic `rail['jobId']`/`rail['status']='running'` (`desktop_repository.dart:74-86`). Per-rail fields read: `rail['railIndex']`, `rail['mode']`, `rail['aiEngine']`, `rail['name']`, `rail['ticketIds']`.
- `POST /v1/projects/:pid/rails/:i/launch` → companion sends body `{mode, profileName?, aiEngine?, model?}` (`desktop_repository.dart:116-123`). The gateway narrows to exactly `{mode, profileName, aiEngine, model}` (`mobile-router.ts:187-197`).
- `PUT /v1/projects/:pid/rails/:i/engine {aiEngine|null}` (`desktop_repository.dart:127-130`; `mobile-router.ts:199-206`).
- `PUT /v1/projects/:pid/rails/:i/name {name|null}` (`desktop_repository.dart:134-137`; `mobile-router.ts:208-215`).
- `PUT /v1/projects/:pid/rails/:i/tickets {ticketIds:int[]}` (`desktop_repository.dart:144-147`; `mobile-router.ts:179-185`).
- `POST /v1/projects/:pid/rails/:i/stop` (`desktop_repository.dart:139-142`; `mobile-router.ts:217-221`).
- Job visibility: `GET /v1/projects/:pid/jobs`, `/jobs/:jid`, `/queue`, and `DELETE /jobs/:jid` (`desktop_repository.dart:27-69, 149-152`). Rail "View running job log" routes to `JobDetailScreen` by `jobId` (`rails_zone.dart:271-281`).

**WS (the bridge in `server/mobile/mobile-ws.ts`):**
- `topicFor()` (`mobile-ws.ts:54-57`) maps `rail.job_started`/`rail.job_stopped`/`rail.job_completed`/`rail.updated` → topic `'rails'`, forwarded **verbatim** (not renamed). `topicFor()` returns `null` for any unrecognised type, and unknown-topic messages are dropped at dispatch (`mobile-ws.ts:210`).
- Companion handles `rail.*` in `project_shell.dart:62-80`: an inbound guard `if (pid != null && pid != widget.projectId && !type.startsWith('hub.')) return;` (`project_shell.dart:62`) project-filters by `msg.projectId`; then `startsWith('rail.')` invalidates rails/jobs providers; the special case `rail.job_completed` with `status=='completed'` + `m['jobId']` fires `NotificationService.jobOutcome` (the "Rail finished" push, `project_shell.dart:70-77`).
- Job-tail: `watch_job {projectId,jobId}` → `log_batch`/`job_event` frames (`mobile-ws.ts:196-243`), keyed by `jobId`. This is the only live-progress channel for a running rail today.

**Schema (`gateway.schema.json`):** a passive, non-load-bearing doc artifact — never imported or validated against in `lib/`. It declares 5 definitions (`QrPayload`, `Project`, `Ticket`, `Job`, `QueueSnapshot`) and **has no rail/loop/mode/ai_engine field at all**. `Job` (`gateway.schema.json:115-169`) has no `loopId`/`loopRunId`/`surface`.

**Models (`models.dart`):** `Job.fromJson` (`models.dart:73-85`) requires only `id`/`command`/`status`; everything else nullable with camel/snake tolerance. No rail model exists.

**The companion's running-state model:** one rail launch ⇒ one `rail.job_started` ⇒ a watchable `jobId`; running is inferred from `activeJobs[railIndex]` or `rail.job_started`; live progress comes only from the `jobId`-keyed `watch_job` log tail; completion from `rail.job_completed` keyed by `jobId`. Every link in this chain is `jobId`-anchored.

## 2. What rails-as-loops changed — the divergence list

- **`loopId` is the new primary launch verb.** `POST /rails/:i/launch` now accepts `{mode='implement', profileName, aiEngine, model, interactive, loopId, reasoning_effort}` (`rails-router.ts:214-215`). `VALID_MODES` is now `{implement, batch-implement, ultracode, loop}` (`rails-router.ts:25`).
- **The mode segmented-control was removed** from the desktop UI and replaced by `RailLoopSelector` (`RailControls.tsx:51-53` comment; `RailRow.tsx:414-421, 597-604`). `RailMode` still exists but is now **derived** from the loop via `deriveRailMode()` (`rail-loops.ts:34-39`), not user-picked.
- **Factory→mode mapping (the compat layer).** Client factory ids `factory:implement|factory:batch|factory:ultracode` (`rail-loops.ts:8-25`); server mirror `loop-factory.ts:33-55`. `factoryLoopMode()` maps `factory:implement→implement`, `factory:batch→batch-implement`, `factory:ultracode→ultracode` (`rails-router.ts:220-224`); any custom loop → `mode='loop'`.
- **Loop runs are NOT job-queue jobs.** When `isLoopsEnabled()` (default ON, `feature-flags.ts:51-52`, `!== 'false'`) AND a `loopId` is present (factory OR custom), the launch routes through **`LoopRunManager`**, not `QueueManager` (`rails-router.ts:301-381`). It returns `202 {loopRunIds, railIndex, mode}` with **no `jobId`** (`rails-router.ts:379`), and rows live in a **separate `loop_runs` table** (`loop-runs-store.ts:12-32`) keyed by `loopRunId`. The legacy ultracode/implement paths still return `{jobId, ...}` (`rails-router.ts:428, 453`).
- **New WS lifecycle family.** `loop.run_started`/`loop.run_progress`/`loop.run_stopped`/`loop.run_completed` (`types.ts:756-790`), emitted by `LoopRunManager` (`loop-run-manager.ts:469`), NOT by the `project-registry.ts:543` `onJobFinished` path that emits `rail.job_completed`. Keying: `loop.run_started`/`loop.run_stopped`/`loop.run_completed` carry `railIndex` + `loopRunId`; **`loop.run_progress` carries only `loopRunId`/`iteration`/`activeNode`/`reasoning` — NO `railIndex`** (`types.ts:756-790`). `loop.run_completed.status ∈ {success, max-iterations, stopped, failed}` — and `max-iterations` is a **successful** terminal state, not a failure.
- **`GET /rails` gained `activeLoopRuns`** → `{rails, activeJobs:{[idx]:{jobId,mode}}, activeLoopRuns:{[idx]:{loopRunId}}}` (`rails-router.ts:78-82`).
- **`loopId`/`effort` are NOT persisted on the rail row.** `RailState` is still `{railIndex, ticketIds, mode, profileName, aiEngine, name}` (`rails-store.ts:3-13`); rails table cols are `rail_index, ticket_id, position, mode, profile_name, ai_engine` (`db.ts:236`), `name` in `rail_meta` (migration 28). `loopId` is purely a per-launch param; `reasoning_effort` persists only on `loop_runs.reasoning_effort`.
- **The actual provider/model a loop ran with is recorded only on `loop_runs`.** A loop launch resolves provider as `railProvider ?? c.project.provider ?? 'claude'` and model as `model || adapter.defaultModel()`; the resolved values are written to `loop_runs.provider`/`loop_runs.model` (`loop-runs-store.ts:12-32`), never back onto the rail row.
- **`reasoning_effort`** (`low|medium|high`) is a new per-launch field (`rails-router.ts:31, 318-324`; client `RailEffortSelector` `RailRow.tsx:422-424`).
- **Standalone loop runs** via `POST /loop-runs` (`project-router-loop-runs.ts:25-87`) exist but are entirely outside the mobile boundary.

**Premise correction (load-bearing):** "loop runs are job-backed (jobId===runId)" is **inaccurate** for this codebase. Factory loops fall back to the `QueueManager` (real `jobId`) path **only when Loops are DISABLED**; with Loops enabled (the default), even factory loops become `loopRunId`-keyed `LoopRunManager` runs (`rails-router.ts:301`). Any reviewer assuming `jobId===runId` will mis-scope the entire fix.

## 3. Does mirror mode still work today? (per capability)

> Behaviour bifurcates on `SPECRAILS_LOOPS_SECTION`. Default is **ON** (`feature-flags.ts:51-52`), so the assessments below are for the default/enabled state. With Loops OFF, every launch reverts to the byte-identical legacy `QueueManager`/`jobId` path and all four capabilities WORK.
>
> **App-Review scoping note:** if the build under review runs in **demo mode** (`demo_repository.dart`), the loop surfaces are invisible to reviewers entirely — demo rails hardcode `mode:'implement'` and `/specrails:implement` commands and never emit `activeLoopRuns`/`loop.run_*`. The frozen-contract risk *during review* for loop surfaces is therefore near-nil; the real, present risk is **post-approval**, when an already-shipped v1 phone connects to a real (default-ON) desktop and silently mis-mirrors. This sharpens the urgency: **Phase 0 desktop forwarding is the only thing that protects phones already in users' hands.**

**(a) VIEW rails list/state — DEGRADED.**
The list fetch never crashes (untyped maps, tolerant parsers). But a rail running a loop reports via `activeLoopRuns` (`rails-router.ts:78-82`), which the companion **does not read** — it folds only `activeJobs` (`desktop_repository.dart:76-86`). So a loop-running rail shows as **idle** (Launch button enabled, no Cancel, no running badge — `rails_zone.dart:72` running = `status==='running'||jobId!=null`). The displayed `rail['mode']` is also stale/misleading: the persisted rail `mode` defaults to `'implement'` (`rails-store.ts:6`) and there is no `loopId`/`loopName` field on the row, so a rail that ran a custom loop renders as `"… · implement · claude"`. Per-rail **engine** display also drifts: the companion shows `rail['aiEngine']` (often null → "default"), but the loop actually ran on `railProvider ?? project.provider ?? 'claude'` with `model || adapter.defaultModel()` (recorded only on `loop_runs.provider`/`.model`, never forwarded) — so a no-override rail running a loop on the project primary shows "default" with no way to surface what the run truly used.

**(b) VIEW a running rail's job/log AND live progress — BROKEN (for loop-backed runs).**
Loop runs have a `loopRunId`, never a `jobId`, and are **not in the jobs/queue tables** (`loop-runs-store.ts:12-32`). The companion's "View running job log" routes by `jobId` (`rails_zone.dart:271-281`); `watch_job`/`log_batch`/`job_event` key on `jobId` (`mobile-ws.ts:196-243`). With no `jobId`, the job-tail surface never populates and the run is absent from Execution History (`JobHistoryScreen` reads queue jobs only). **Critically, a loop run produces NO tailable log at all** — its sole live heartbeat is `loop.run_progress` (`iteration`/`activeNode`), which is dropped at `topicFor()`. So even discounting the job-log routing, there is **no live-progress channel** for a running loop rail today: the running surface is a binary running/idle black box. For legacy non-loop launches the job-tail still WORKS.

**(c) LAUNCH a rail — WORKS (factory/legacy only) / BROKEN (custom loops).**
The companion sends bare `{mode}` (`rails_zone.dart:317` picker = `implement|batch-implement|ultracode`; `desktop_repository.dart:116-123`). This still validates server-side (`VALID_MODES` includes the three; default `mode='implement'` at `rails-router.ts:214`). Crucially, the gateway narrowing **strips `loopId`** (`mobile-router.ts:191-196`), so even a future companion that sent `loopId` would be silently ignored. Custom loops are unreachable (`mode='loop'` without `loopId` → 400, `rails-router.ts:385-386`). **Caveat:** the *running-state feedback* after launch is broken per (a)/(b) when the launch resolves to a `LoopRunManager` run (default-ON factory loops emit `loop.run_*`, no `rail.job_started`) — so the launch HTTP call succeeds (202) but the phone sees no live activity, no progress, and no completion notification.

**(d) Stop / assign tickets / engine — DEGRADED (stop) / WORKS (tickets) / WORKS-with-display-drift (engine).**
- **Engine:** `PUT /rails/:i/engine {aiEngine}` WORKS end-to-end for *setting* the override (`desktop_repository.dart:127`; `mobile-router.ts:199-206`); `rail.updated` carries `aiEngine` (`types.ts:749`). The mutation needs no change. **But** the *displayed* engine drifts for loop-backed runs as noted in (a): the rail config `aiEngine` may be null while the actual run used the resolved provider/model from `loop_runs`, which is never forwarded.
- **Tickets:** `PUT /rails/:i/tickets {ticketIds}` WORKS (gateway narrows to `ticketIds`; upstream `getRail()` preserves `mode/profile/engine` — `rails-router.ts:108-114`).
- **Stop:** `POST /rails/:i/stop` server-side DOES cancel all jobs **and** all loop runs for the rail (`rails-router.ts:467` → `{jobIds, loopRunIds, canceled}`). So the call works, but the companion never offers the Stop affordance for a loop run because it shows the rail as idle (a)/(b). Hence **DEGRADED**: the action is correct but unreachable in the UI for loop-backed rails.

## 4. Required changes — DESKTOP WIRE (`server/mobile/*`), additive + frozen-safe

All changes below are **purely additive** — they add new fields/types/topics-onto-existing-topic and do not touch any frozen string (`specrailshub`, `hub`/`hubName`/`hubInstanceId`, `hub.*`, `hub_daily_budget_exceeded`, the `hubDailySpend`/`hubBudget` budget renames, `LEGACY_WIRE_TYPES`, the `'rails'` topic name, the bare-`mode` launch path).

**4.1 Forward `loopId` (and effort/interactive) on launch.**
`server/mobile/mobile-router.ts:187-197` — extend the launch-body narrowing. After the existing `mode/profileName/aiEngine/model` fields:
```
if (typeof b.loopId === 'string') narrowed.loopId = b.loopId;
if (b.reasoning_effort === 'low' || b.reasoning_effort === 'medium' || b.reasoning_effort === 'high') narrowed.reasoning_effort = b.reasoning_effort;
if (typeof b.interactive === 'boolean') narrowed.interactive = b.interactive;
```
Purely additive to the `narrowed` object; the frozen bare-`mode` default at `rails-router.ts:214` is untouched and still server-accepted. This is the single prerequisite that unlocks any mobile custom/factory-loop launch; until it lands, the gateway silently drops `loopId`.

**4.2 Add loop read routes to the allow-list (catalog AND running/per-run state).**
`mobile-router.ts:366-399` (`MOBILE_ALLOWLIST`) — add GET entries forwarding to the desktop loops store:
- `GET /api/projects/:pid/loops` (and `GET /api/projects/:pid/loops/factory`) — the catalog backing `RailLoopSelector`, needed to build a picker.
- `GET /api/projects/:pid/loop-runs/:id` (and/or a per-rail active loop-run state read) — needed for the **running** surface (5.3's progress view has nothing to GET without it) AND for any future Execution-History parity.

**CI note:** `MOBILE_ALLOWLIST` is asserted by a drift test to resolve against a *real* internal route — each new entry must point at an existing desktop route, so the desktop `GET /loops`, `GET /loops/factory`, and `GET /loop-runs/:id` routes must exist before (or in the same change as) the allow-list append, or the drift test fails. The frozen-string regression guards (grep-based, for `hub.*`/`specrailshub`/budget renames) plus this drift test together enforce the additivity claim — point a CI reviewer at both as the guardrails of record.

**4.3 Surface loop identity on the rail GET shape (upstream desktop gap first).**
`activeLoopRuns` already crosses verbatim through `redact()`. To label *which* loop a rail is bound to, the **upstream** rail shape needs `loopId`/`loopName` — but `RailState` has no such field (`rails-store.ts:3-13`) and it isn't persisted. Recommended minimal approach without a schema migration: enrich the `activeLoopRuns` map entries to `{loopRunId, loopId, loopName, provider, model}` in `rails-router.ts:78-82` (resolved from the `loop_runs` row, which already has `loop_id`/`loop_name`/`provider`/`model` — `loop-runs-store.ts:12-32`). This is additive on the GET response and reaches mobile through the generic `projectReads` forward (`mobile-router.ts:129`). Forwarding `provider`/`model` here also fixes the engine display-drift in 3(a)/3(d). **Limitation:** this only labels a rail *while a run is active*; a configured-but-idle rail has no persisted loop binding to display (upstream desktop limitation, not mobile-only).

**4.4 Translate `loop.run_*` WS to the existing `'rails'` topic.**
`server/mobile/mobile-ws.ts` `topicFor()` (`:44-75`) — add cases mapping `loop.run_started`/`loop.run_progress`/`loop.run_stopped`/`loop.run_completed` → `'rails'`. **Reusing the existing `'rails'` topic is the only frozen-safe choice** — it keeps the companion subscribe set (`project_shell.dart:43`: `{queue,tickets,rails,phase,spending,activity,alerts,chat}`) unchanged. Introducing a NEW topic name would be gated out at dispatch (`mobile-ws.ts:210`, unknown topic → dropped) unless the frozen subscribe set is also changed — do NOT do that.

`loop.run_progress` is **load-bearing, not optional**: it is the *sole* live heartbeat for a loop run (no tailable log exists), so forwarding it is the only way the running surface can show any progress at all. Forward `iteration`/`activeNode` (and `loopRunId`/`status`/`railIndex` where present) — but see 4.5 for the `reasoning` field.

Two valid strategies:
- **(Preferred, additive) Forward the new types verbatim** under `'rails'`. An old v1 companion's `startsWith('rail.')` branch will NOT match `loop.run_*`, so it harmlessly ignores them (no crash); updated companions parse `loopRunId`/`status`/`iteration`/`activeNode`. No frozen string touched.
- **(Compat-synthesis, NOT frozen-clean-by-default) Synthesize a `rail.job_started`-shaped frame** at loop launch with `jobId = loopRunId` and a derived `mode`. This is the ONLY proposed item that fabricates a frozen-typed frame: a v1 companion would then route "View running job log" to `watch_job`/`log_batch` keyed on a fake `jobId` (`mobile-ws.ts:196-243`) that has **no tailable log** → a dead/empty job-tail. If shipped at all, it MUST also suppress/guard the v1 job-tail route for synthetic ids. **Prefer verbatim-forward; treat compat-synthesis as a deliberate, guarded exception, not the default.**

**4.5 Redaction — DROP `reasoning` in the mobile mapping.**
`redact()` (`mobile-redact.ts:16,44-81`) strips only `$HOME`/absolute-path tokens; `loopId`/`loopRunId`/`mode`/`aiEngine`/`status`/`iteration`/`activeNode` pass through fine. **But `loop.run_progress.reasoning` (`types.ts:771-772`) is free-text LLM output and is NOT scrubbed for repo content** — forwarding it verbatim would surface more repo content to the phone than any current `rail.*` frame, creating a new exfiltration surface the existing redactor does not cover. **This MUST be applied:** drop the `reasoning` field in the loop→mobile mapping (forward only `iteration`/`activeNode`) unless a content-redaction pass is added. This is the one place where naive "forward verbatim" is unsafe.

**Do NOT need:** `/rails/:i/profile` and `/rails/:i/name` already absent from the allow-list for mutation; not required for the mirror pass (the companion can display name/profile from `rail.updated`).

## 5. Required changes — COMPANION (Flutter)

**5.1 `lib/data/models.dart` — add a tolerant rail/loop view.**
Extending `Job.fromJson` tolerance (`models.dart:73-85`) is unnecessary (loop runs aren't jobs). The concrete need is in the repository layer (5.2). Optionally introduce a typed `Rail`/`LoopRun` model with nullable `loopId`, `loopName`, `loopRunId`, `effort`, `provider`, `model`, `iteration`, `activeNode` alongside `mode`/`aiEngine`.

**5.2 `lib/data/desktop_repository.dart` — read `activeLoopRuns`.**
`rails()` (`:71-88`) currently folds only `activeJobs` into `rail['status']`/`rail['jobId']`. Extend the fold (around `:76-86`): for each `activeLoopRuns[railIndex]`, set `rail['status']='running'`, `rail['loopRunId']=...`, and (per 4.3) `rail['loopId']`/`rail['loopName']`/`rail['provider']`/`rail['model']`. This is the single change that fixes the phantom-idle bug. Also widen `launchRail` (`:116-123`) to send `loopId` (and optionally `reasoning_effort`/`interactive`) when a loop is picked.

**5.3 `lib/features/jobs/rails_zone.dart` — loop name/provider instead of mode picker; live progress.**
- Tile subtitle (`:73-74, :87`) and sheet "Mode:" line (`:151, :218`): render `rail['loopName'] ?? rail['mode']` so a loop-running rail shows the loop identity, not stale `implement`. For engine, prefer the forwarded `rail['provider']`/`rail['model']` (4.3) over the possibly-null config `aiEngine`.
- Running detection (`:72`): include `rail['loopRunId'] != null` so loop-running rails show Cancel, not Launch.
- **Live-progress view:** for loop-backed rails, render `iteration`/`activeNode` from `loop.run_progress` (forwarded per 4.4) and/or poll `GET /v1/.../loop-runs/:id` (4.2) — this is the replacement for the `jobId` log tail that loop runs will never have. Do NOT route "View running job log" (`:271-281`) to `JobDetailScreen` by a null `jobId`; disable it or route to the loop-run progress view.
- Launch picker (`confirmLaunchRail`, `:308-354, :317`): replace the hardcoded `implement|batch-implement|ultracode` bottom-sheet with a **Loop picker** populated from the new loop-catalog endpoint (4.2). Send `loopId` (factory or custom). Keep a fallback to bare `mode` for old-desktop compat (see phasing). For factory loops, the picker can offer the three factory ids (`factory:implement|factory:batch|factory:ultracode`).

**5.4 WS handlers for loop runs — `lib/features/project/project_shell.dart`.**
`project_shell.dart:62-80` handles `rail.*` only. Add a `startsWith('loop.run_')` branch **inside** the existing inbound guard (`:62`, the `projectId`-filter) — loop runs ARE `projectId`-scoped (carried via `boundBroadcast`) so they pass the filter; read `m['projectId']` consistently so the branch isn't accidentally gated. The branch must: (a) invalidate `railsProvider`/`jobsProvider` (same as `rail.*` at `:67`); (b) on `loop.run_completed`, fire `NotificationService.jobOutcome` mapping the **success set `{success, max-iterations}`** → success (note `max-iterations` is a *successful* terminal state, NOT a failure — a naive `ok = status=='success'` mislabels it), mirroring the `rail.job_completed`/`status=='completed'` path at `:70-77`, using `loopRunId`/`ticketIds`.
- **`railIndex` caveat:** `loop.run_started`/`loop.run_stopped`/`loop.run_completed` carry `railIndex`, but `loop.run_progress` carries only `loopRunId` (no `railIndex`). A handler keying live progress by `railIndex` must first map `loopRunId → railIndex` from `activeLoopRuns` (or from a prior `loop.run_started`).
- Subscribe set (`:43`) needs **no** change if loop types are mapped onto `'rails'` (4.4).

**5.5 Repository endpoints.**
Add `loops(pid)` → `GET /v1/projects/:pid/loops` (and `loopsFactory`/`GET /loops/factory`) to feed the picker, and `loopRun(pid, id)` → `GET /v1/projects/:pid/loop-runs/:id` to feed the running-progress view — both consuming the new allow-list entries from 4.2.

**5.6 `gateway.schema.json` (optional, doc-only).**
Non-load-bearing, but to keep it honest: add a `Rail` definition (`railIndex, ticketIds[], mode, profileName?, aiEngine?, name?, loopId?, loopName?, provider?, model?`), an optional `Loop`/`LoopRun` definition, and `activeLoopRuns` to a `RailsSnapshot`. Add `loopRunId?` to `Job` only if loop runs ever surface there (they don't today). This changes nothing at runtime but removes the false sense of contract.

**5.7 Launch-payload change.**
From `{mode}` → `{loopId}` (with `mode` retained as fallback). Custom loops require `loopId`; factory loops can send either `loopId='factory:…'` or bare `mode` (both validate server-side). Gate the picker behind a feature check (loop-catalog endpoint present, 4.2) so it degrades to the mode picker against an old desktop.

## 6. Stays FROZEN / must NOT change

These are intact in the redesign and **must remain** so (v1 in App Review):
- mDNS service type `'specrailshub'`.
- QR / pairing payload field names: `hub`, `hubName`, `hubInstanceId` (`gateway.schema.json:5-50`; `signaling.dart:65-72`; `desktop_connection.dart:25-31`; `pairing_service.dart:62-71`).
- Legacy outbound WS types: `hub.projects`, `hub.project_added`, `hub.project_removed`, `hub_daily_budget_exceeded`, and the budget field renames `hubDailySpend`/`hubBudget` — all via `LEGACY_WIRE_TYPES`/`toMobileWire` (`mobile-ws.ts:83-100`). **Do not rename.**
- The existing `rail.job_started`/`rail.job_stopped`/`rail.job_completed`/`rail.updated` shapes and the `'rails'` topic name (`mobile-ws.ts:54-57`) — forwarded verbatim, keep stable.
- The bare-`mode` launch path must remain server-accepted (`rails-router.ts:214` default `mode='implement'`): it is the only launch verb a v1 companion can emit. Do **not** force `loopId`-only on `/rails/:i/launch`.
- The frozen subscribe topic set on the companion (`project_shell.dart:43`) — only extend if a genuinely new topic is introduced (which this design deliberately avoids by mapping loop types onto `'rails'`).

---

## 7. Recommended phasing

**Phase 0 — Desktop-only "keep mirror honest" (no companion release, frozen-safe). HIGHEST URGENCY.**
This is the only thing that protects **already-shipped v1 phones in users' hands** the moment they connect to a default-ON desktop. Ship 4.1–4.5 on the desktop: forward `loop.run_*` verbatim under `'rails'` (4.4, dropping `reasoning` per 4.5), enrich `activeLoopRuns` with `loopName`/`provider`/`model` (4.3), and add the loop read routes (4.2). Even **without** a companion update, an old companion ignores the unknown WS types harmlessly and continues launching factory modes. Optional: if you want a v1 phone to show running/finished for loop rails *before* a companion ship, use the **compat-synthesis** option (4.4) — but it fabricates `jobId=loopRunId` and breaks the v1 job-tail, so ship it only with the synthetic-id job-tail guard, and decide deliberately.

**Phase 1 — Minimal "loop-backed rails as runs" companion pass (recommended first companion release).**
Companion treats loop-backed rails as runs without a full loop builder: read `activeLoopRuns` (5.2), show `loopName`/forwarded provider instead of stale mode/null-engine (5.3 display only), handle `loop.run_*` for running/progress/completed + notification with the `{success, max-iterations}` success set (5.4), and render `iteration`/`activeNode` for live progress. **No loop picker yet** — launch still sends bare `mode` for the three factory equivalents. This fixes the three real correctness defects (phantom-idle, no-live-progress, missing completion notification) with the smallest surface, and keeps the mirror "non-misleading."

**Phase 2 — Full "loops on mobile".**
Add the loop-catalog/loop-run read routes (4.2/5.5), the Loop picker UI (5.3), and `loopId` launch (5.7), plus effort/interactive forwarding (4.1). This is the only phase that lets a phone launch a **custom** user-built loop. Gate the picker behind a feature check (loop-catalog endpoint present) so it degrades to the mode picker against an old desktop. Update `demo_repository.dart` in lockstep (demo `activeLoopRuns` + demo loop catalog) so App-Review demo mode reflects the new model.

---

## 8. Risks

- **App-Review frozen-contract pitfall.** Any fix that renames a frozen string (`specrailshub`, `hub`/`hubName`/`hubInstanceId`, `hub.*`, `hub_daily_budget_exceeded`, `hubDailySpend`/`hubBudget`) breaks the v1 app under review. Mitigation: all loop work is additive — new fields, new WS types mapped onto the **existing** `'rails'` topic, new allow-list entries. Never touch `LEGACY_WIRE_TYPES` (`mobile-ws.ts:83-88`). The grep-based frozen-string guards + the `MOBILE_ALLOWLIST` drift test are the CI guardrails that enforce this — confirm both stay green.

- **Version skew — new desktop + old companion (the default today).** With Loops ON, factory launches go through `LoopRunManager` and emit only `loop.run_*` (`rails-router.ts:301-381`), which the old boundary drops (`topicFor` default→null, `mobile-ws.ts:210`). Result: rails launched from the phone (or desktop) show **no live activity, no live progress, and no completion push** on an old companion, and loop-running rails read as **idle** (`activeLoopRuns` ignored). This is a silent correctness regression, not a crash. Because App-Review may see only demo mode, the regression bites **post-approval on shipped phones** — making Phase 0 desktop forwarding the urgent item.

- **Version skew — new companion + old desktop.** A new companion sending `loopId` against an old gateway: the old `mobile-router.ts:191-196` strips `loopId`, desktop falls to bare-`mode` → user "selected a loop" but got legacy `implement` with no error. Mitigation: companion must feature-detect the loop-catalog endpoint (4.2) before showing the picker, and always retain the bare-`mode` fallback.

- **`reasoning` leak (must-fix).** `loop.run_progress.reasoning` (`types.ts:771-772`) is unredacted free-text LLM output; `redact()` only scrubs paths (`mobile-redact.ts:16,44-81`). Forwarding it verbatim surfaces more repo content to the phone than any current `rail.*` frame. Mitigation: drop `reasoning` in the mobile mapping (4.5).

- **Compat-synthesis fabricates a frozen-typed frame.** The optional 4.4 compat-synthesis (synthesize `rail.job_started` with `jobId=loopRunId`) is the only proposed item that injects a value into the frozen `jobId` slot; a v1 phone then tails a non-existent log → dead job-tail. Not frozen-clean-by-default; ship only with a synthetic-id job-tail guard.

- **`demo_repository.dart` drift.** Demo rails hardcode `mode:'implement'` and demo jobs use `/specrails:implement` commands (`demo_repository.dart:102-130`); no `activeLoopRuns`. If the companion UI moves to loop names/pickers, the demo fixtures must be updated in lockstep — and demo mode is exactly what reviewers see. Add demo `activeLoopRuns` + a demo loop catalog when Phase 2 ships.

- **`loopId`/`effort` not persisted on the rail.** `RailState`/rails table have no loop column (`rails-store.ts:3-13`, `db.ts:236`). The mirror can only show the loop while a run is active (via `activeLoopRuns` + `loop_runs` join, 4.3); a *configured-but-not-running* rail has no loop binding to display. Upstream desktop limitation, not a mobile-only gap.

- **Per-rail engine/provider display drift.** The companion shows config `aiEngine` (often null → "default"), but a loop runs on `railProvider ?? project.provider ?? 'claude'` + `model || adapter.defaultModel()` (recorded only on `loop_runs.provider`/`.model`). Without forwarding provider/model (4.3), the mirror cannot show what a loop-backed run actually used. The engine *mutation* path is fine; only *display* drifts.

- **Job-history blindness persists.** Loop runs live in `loop_runs`, not `jobs`/`queue` (`loop-runs-store.ts:12-32`), so they will not appear in the companion's Execution History or `Job`-model cost surfacing from WS fixes alone. The `GET /loop-runs/:id` read route (4.2) feeds the *running* surface; full history parity additionally needs a list route + a `LoopRun` model — flag as a follow-up beyond the mirror passes.

- **Single point holding mobile launch alive.** The factory→legacy-mode mapping (`rails-router.ts:220-224`) plus the bare-`mode` default (`:214`) is the only thing keeping the v1 companion's launch working. If desktop ever removes bare-`mode` acceptance, the companion's `{mode}`-only `launchRail` (`desktop_repository.dart:116-123`) 400s. Treat bare-`mode` acceptance as frozen.
